_comment: Which cases of the shared Lua contracts moved into JSON vector corpora (PAR-58). Each moved entry names the removed case (an it title, or a loop's title prefix) and the vector ids that now hold it. tools/test/test-contract-vector-ledger.cjs fails when a vector is not listed here, when a listed vector is missing, when a removed case title is still registered in its contract, or when a vector breaks the schema. contracts: for every remaining Lua contract of the families (config_scope_*, toml_*, menu_*), data_driven lists the registration sites fed by a JSON corpus and stays_in_lua lists each other registration site with the reason it stays Lua (reasons below); lua_sites is the number of registration sites (helpers.it( or test("), so a new Lua case without a ledger entry fails the gate. Reasons were assigned by reviewing the cases of the toml_* and config_scope_plan contracts and by rule (identity, metatables, patched functions, the family of the contract) for the rest.

field_semantics.entry_point: Descriptive: names the one function a port's consumer must call for the family's vectors; read by people, checked by tools/test/test-contract-vector-ledger.cjs only for presence of the family.
field_semantics.windows_consumer: Descriptive: what the AutoHotkey consumer of the family does with each vector; no replay reads it.
field_semantics.row_corpus: Descriptive: the corpus that already holds the menu rows a Lua contract's ordered-callback cases are about; read by people porting the assertions as code.

reasons.lua_identity: Asserts the identity of a closure or table (rawequal) or mutates a returned table to prove it was a copy. A port asserts identity with its own references.
reasons.lua_hooks: Proves user-controlled metatable hooks (__index, __len, __eq, __tostring, __pairs) are never run. Lua-only mechanism: the AutoHotkey equivalent (__Get, __Enum, __Call) needs its own test.
reasons.lua_table_shape: Depends on Lua table shapes JSON cannot carry (a sparse array, a hole, a named key in an array).
reasons.fault_injection: Replaces a production function (an encoder, a codec, a loaded module) to force a fault, then repairs it. A port injects faults its own way.
reasons.ordered_callbacks: Asserts which injected getters, actions or participants ran and in which order, around menu rows that are already JSON where row_corpus names the corpus. The Windows side ports the assertions as code over the same rows.
reasons.transaction_sequence: A multi-step apply, revert or retry with retained debt, reentrancy or settlement order across participants.
reasons.file_effects: Backup, publication and restoration of real or virtual files and the exact bytes of several files.
reasons.in_memory_document: Encodes against a decoded document and its shape receipt after the test mutated the Lua table in between.
reasons.internal_api: Calls an internal module surface directly (scanner records, span evidence, planner row counts, script projection, sequences whose output feeds the next step) whose shape is the Lua module's own; data in principle once that surface is a named entry point.
reasons.global_state: Depends on a process-wide writer registry (refuse_writes, sparse defaults).
reasons.generated_manifest: Asserts over the generated manifest data itself, not over inputs; Windows shares the generated manifest and should gate it by its own check.
reasons.snapshot_argument: Needs two different sources (the hint source and the source read afterwards) or a global fence; data in principle with a second source field.
